articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Bayern's Karl to get 'dream' Real Madrid move?
articles.description: Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid, while AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are keeping tabs on Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl, according to Bild's Christian Falk. Los Blancos are among several teams interested in the 18-year-old, with whom the Bundesliga champions plan to open contract renewal talks, while rival clubs monitor whether Michael Olise's presence in his position could create a transfer opportunity. Karl said during an event in January that playing for Madrid would be a "dream" which led to an apology after the comments sparked anger among Bayern fans.

- AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract extending until the summer of 2031, according to Corriere dello Sport. Initial talks have begun with the 28-year-old's representatives over a deal worth around €5 million per season following his goal-scoring performance in Sunday's 3-0 win over Lecce.

- Chelsea are considering Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Feyenoord's Gjivai Zechiël as potential successors to Enzo Fernández, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old Zechiel has registered five goals and four assists in seven Eredivisie matches this season, attracting interest from Chelsea, Liverpool, and five other Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri is being scouted by Juventus, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The 25-year-old tops the Bianconeri shortlist for the January transfer window, with a loan approach lined up due to his lack of playing time under Enzo Maresca, while RB Leipzig's David Raum is considered an alternative.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are interested in Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae, according to Christian Falk. Both clubs have tracked the 29-year-old South Korea international since the summer, though any move is expected to depend on upcoming contract discussions with the German club.

Other rumors

- Arsenal are among four Premier League teams tracking Sturm Graz midfielder Luca Weinhandl, 17. (TEAMtalk)

- Barcelona sent scouts to watch Athletico Paranaense defender Arthur Dias in their 2-1 victory over Bahia on Sunday. (Sport)

- Bayern Munich are not considering a move for Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade, who is currently on loan at Juventus, despite recent reports. (Christian Falk)

- Liverpool, Arsenal, and Chelsea are among the clubs tracking Real Sociedad defender Jon Martín. (Ekrem Konur)

- Aston Villa are preparing contract extension talks with attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía. (Daily Mail)

- Roma and AC Milan are lining up a loan approach for Real Madrid striker Endrick in January. (Calciomercato)

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026: The new top 10 features a razor-thin race for No. 1
articles.description: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players hits its grand finale.
articles.body:
Welcome to the grand finale of NBA Rank 2026.

After unveiling Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday and Nos. 50-11 on Wednesday, the big reveal is here.

Who will be the top 10 players for the 2026-27 season? How high did reigning Finals MVP Jalen Brunson climb? Did Victor Wembanyama just begin a LeBron James-esque run atop of the list?

While ESPN's latest top 10 -- err, full top 100 -- will surely spark debate, what can't be questioned is the remarkably tight race for this season's No. 1 spot. Just three voting points separated Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wembanyama, with each superstar placing atop at least one of the seven panelists' individual rankings.

That panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition. In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven NBA experts: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list -- the best of the best heading into the new NBA season.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

10. Donovan Mitchell

G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 15

Mitchell rises into the top 10 after leading the Cavaliers to the Eastern Conference finals last season, his first such appearance in his nine-year career. He has finished in the top seven in MVP voting in three of the past four seasons, and his ability to create off the dribble while using his shooting range to freeze defenders makes him the offensive force of the Cavs. Mitchell has been an All-Star in seven straight seasons, and he pairs with James Harden to give Cleveland one of the few backcourts where each starter boasts multiple All-NBA selections. 

Biggest question: Can Mitchell be the best player on a champion?

The Cavaliers start four All-Stars in Mitchell, Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, but in the playoffs they will go only as far as Mitchell can lead them.

One of the ironies of Mitchell's first run to the conference finals was that he didn't play particularly well compared to past postseasons. In his six playoffs runs from 2020 to 2025, Mitchell averaged 30.0 points per game with a player efficiency rating (PER) of 24.5. Last season, he averaged 26.0 points with a PER of just 18.6 (15.0 is considered average). The former version is absolutely good enough to carry the Cavs back to the Finals, especially if Mitchell sees a repeat performance from his teammates. -- André Snellings

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026 audit: What we got right -- and wrong -- in our top 100
articles.description: Using an analytical lens, Dean Oliver examines what the NBA Rank panel got right -- and what it got very wrong.
articles.body:
When combing through ESPN's latest countdown of the top 100 NBA players, try to remember one phrase, which is just as applicable to ranking players as it is to building a winning roster.

People see the game better than numbers, but numbers see all the games.

As it relates to NBA Rank 2026, those numbers are a collective of advanced player ratings commonly in use, from ESPN's Net Points to DARKO, LEBRON, EPM and RAPM. Those systems can provide a useful counter perspective to the humans, with their good eyes but occasional biases.

With the full top 100 unveiled for the 2026-27 season, let's examine what the metrics revealed about which player rankings our panelists got right -- and which they got wrong.

Four things NBA Rank got wrong

1. Jalen Brunson (No. 6)

Our last view of Brunson is him carrying the Knicks to a fourth-quarter comeback in Game 5 of the NBA Finals. He was tremendous in New York's run to the championship -- but that leads to the bias that he will maintain it.

He was Finals MVP, but will he really finish the season as the league's sixth-best player? Brunson has always been limited a bit by his size (6-foot-2, 190 pounds) and his defense, something the metrics perhaps see and remember more than the seven panelists remember the late buckets he poured in to win the Finals. Those problems are likely to persist.

I love Brunson's game, but his lofty ranking benefitted not only from recent bias but also from the New York media bias. (That bias might also help you forget that Brunson missed the shot in the most iconic image from the Finals, when OG Anunoby swooped in for the putback game-winner to clinch Game 4.)

The metrics place Brunson around the No. 25 range heading into the season. That's not a huge gap. He's elite, just not No. 6 -- at least not during the regular season.

2. Rookies

Another bias comes from wanting to believe the hype. AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson all make the top 100, but rookies are generally bad NBA players -- predraft highlights don't show the turnovers, or the missed boxouts, or the poor defense.

Is it possible one or two rookies end the year in the top 100 of Net Points per game, per 100 possessions, or another metric? Of course. It's a strong draft, but history suggests these rankings could be a year too early.

3. Jaylen Brown (No. 14)

Without the rehabbing Jayson Tatum, the Celtics were picked to win about 40 games last year, so their overperformance led to a Coach of the Year award for Joe Mazzulla and to a shower of praise for Brown.

The claims of Brown being the league's "best two-way player" came mostly after he had his best game of the year against the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, but few noticed Brown's next game, where he scored 14 points on 24 field goal attempts. Maybe we term this a "highlight bias" because our voters perhaps saw those highlights and loved him, ranking Brown between No. 9 and No. 23. The metrics' average, meanwhile, was around No. 60.

articles.headline: NFL Week 3 uniforms: Colts to wear 'Anvil Strike,' Bills debut 'Nickel City'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 3, led by the new NFL Rivalries look from the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Tuesday marked the first day of fall. The blue skies across the country will turn to gray with the colder months approaching. But to spot a more immediate gray shade, look no further than NFL uniforms in Week 3 -- namely, the Indianapolis Colts and Buffalo Bills. 

Indianapolis will debut its Rivalries uniform against the Houston Texans. Nicknamed "Anvil Strike," they are inspired by the steel of an anvil and the jersey's "dark anthracite" color is one that "embodies the grit and intensity of Colts football." The all-gray threads are complete with a metallic blue helmet. For the first time in team history, the Colts' horseshoe is included on one of their uniforms -- a silver version appears on the sleeve. Other uniform elements are classic blue numbers and "For The Shoe" on the inside collar. The Colts are the first team to debut the latest batch of Rivalries uniforms this season. 

Buffalo is similarly wearing all-gray when it faces the Los Angeles Chargers at home. The "Nickel City" uniforms are a tribute to the "strength, grit and authenticity" of Western New York. The all-gray design is directly inspired by the Buffalo Nickel, a coin minted from 1913 to 1938. A metallic royal blue "charge" helmet tops the look. The helmet's design is meant to bring a charging buffalo to life with the horn, eye and charge streak displayed in red. 

The Denver Broncos will wear their midnight navy alternate look on "Sunday Night Football" against the Los Angeles Rams. Denver first introduced the look ahead of the 2024 season and is 2-0 in the all-navy combination. Last year, the Broncos paired their summit white helmet with the threads, but they'll go with a navy-colored lid this time around.

In the throwback space, the Jacksonville Jaguars are rocking their classic prowler design. First unveiled in 2024, the teal uniforms include a prowling jaguar on the sleeves and a black helmet with the franchises' original primary logo on it. The numbers boast a custom font in white with a black and gold trim. A similar three-color accent runs down the white pants in a teal stripe with gold and black trim.

articles.headline: Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender David Alaba
articles.description: Former Real Madrid defender David Alaba officially signed for Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.
articles.body:
Former Real Madrid defender David Alaba officially signed for Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.

The 34-year-old has been a free agent since his contract with Real Madrid expired at the end of last season.

He spent five years with the LaLiga giants, winning 11 trophies including two Champions Leagues, two league titles and two FIFA Club World Cups.

"Signing David Alaba is a source of immense satisfaction for the entire club," GM Franco Collavino said in a news release. "We are welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival shows Udinese's determination to grow and compete at the highest level as well as build an increasingly ambitious squad."

The defender suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament injury in 2023 which required surgery and his minutes became limited.

Alaba had also previously spent 13 years with German club Bayern Munich, where he won 10 Bundesliga titles and two Champions Leagues.

"I've had many experiences and won a lot over the course of my career, but one thing hasn't changed, I still want to win," Alaba said in the Serie A club's news release. "I still want to compete. And I still want to achieve something special. That is the mindset I'm bringing to Udinese.

"The coach [Kosta Runjaić] made it very clear what role he has in mind for me and what he wants us to achieve together. Naturally, I want to bring my experience to the dressing room, take on responsibility, and help out whenever possible, especially with the younger players.

"I'm not coming here just to be the veteran of the squad, and I certainly didn't come here to wind down my career. I'm still too ambitious for that, and I still strongly believe in what I can do on the pitch. 

"I want to keep pushing, perform at the highest level in Serie A week in and week out, and achieve something meaningful. I'm really excited about this challenge, and I still have a lot to prove to myself."

Alaba has also made 117 appearances for his country, Austria, and captained the side at the World Cup this summer.

Udinese are currently 13th in the Serie A table with four points after five games, and have lost their last three.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Marc Cucurella 'sent a subtle message' to try to tempt Rodri into Real Madrid move
articles.description: Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella has said he "sent a subtle message" asking Rodri to join him at Real Madrid this summer, before the midfielder opted to sign for rivals Barcelona.
articles.body:
Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella has said he "sent a subtle message" asking Rodri to join him at Real Madrid this summer, before the midfielder opted to sign for rivals Barcelona.

Madrid were close to landing Rodri from Manchester City as part of their major rebuild ahead of this season, but Spain's World Cup-winning captain chose to move to Barça instead -- with Hansi Flick's side now six points clear at the top of the LaLiga table.

Both players are now with the Spain squad preparing for Saturday's Nations League game against England and Wembley, and -- speaking to Cadena SER radio -- Cucurella admitted he'd made it clear to Rodri that he'd like to have him as a teammate at the Bernabéu.

"I don't really like pressuring or influencing teammates," Cucurella said. "These are personal things. It's true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we'd become teammates.

"He replied, but didn't give anything away. I'm happy for him [at Barça], though I hope he doesn't have too much success."

Cucurella was one of six new signings at Madrid, joining new coach José Mourinho, but the team are facing criticism after suffering two losses already, at Real Betis and in last weekend's derby with Atlético Madrid.

"We didn't finish the period before the break in the best way," Cucurella said. "It's all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation... Let's see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start."

Atletico targeted Madrid's left-flank, made up of Cucurella and Vinícius Júnior, repeatedly in the derby.

- Barcelona follow Real Madrid in breaking €1 billion revenue barrier

- Real Madrid conspiracy claims dismissed as a 'smokescreen' by LaLiga president

- Lamine Yamal rejects goal stats for Ballon d'Or for 'players that make you dream'

"It's good playing with Vini, but ultimately, we've barely had any training time," Cucurella said. "Connecting with me is different compared to other full-backs, but it's a process. From what I see, and with the effort he's putting in -- knowing it's not his natural strength -- Vinicius is really doing his part."

Statistics show Madrid's players cover less total distance than their LaLiga rivals so far this season, but Cucurella denied that that's a problem.

"That stat surprised me," he said. "But we do run a lot. We're talking about these figures because we lost the derby against Atleti. If we hadn't lost, no one would be mentioning it."

articles.headline: Reranking the men's basketball recruiting class of 2024
articles.description: Cooper Flagg remains No. 1 in this high school class -- but we admit to some mistakes for the rest of the list.
articles.body:
Evaluating and projecting high school recruits is an inexact science. Talent evaluators, scouts, coaches and NBA front offices all have notable hits, along with misses. We're always looking ahead with an eye on potential. But this time, we're looking back at the top of the 2024 SC Next 100 class.

This group had some obvious stars, even at the time, such as Cooper Flagg. But there were also some less obvious risers we perhaps should've picked up on. Kon Knueppel was a productive high schooler with upside; we didn't see him taking off this quickly. The same goes for Jeremiah Fears, a five-star junior who reclassified late and, in hindsight, was slotted too low in the final player rankings.

Injuries, role changes and development can make projecting high school players especially difficult. Now, two years later, this analysis has incorporated their overall résumé to date. So, how did we do in 2024?

Note: Khaman Maluach and Egor Demin, five-star talents who would normally fit among this group, are not eligible because they played their high school basketball outside the United States.

1. Cooper Flagg, SF

2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 1
Flagg was different from a young age. The Maine native reclassified after his sophomore year and eventually ascended to No. 1 in the rankings, then led Montverde Academy to an undefeated season and a Chipotle Nationals championship. "He had zero ego and never complained," said Kevin Boyle Jr., Flagg's associate head coach at Montverde. "He knew when to get his teammates involved and only cared about winning." At Duke, Flagg averaged 19.2 points, 7.5 rebounds and 4.5 assists while leading the Blue Devils to the Final Four. He became just the fourth freshman to win national player of the year, before going No. 1 in the 2025 NBA draft and earning NBA Rookie of the Year honors with the Dallas Mavericks.

2. Dylan Harper, PG

2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 4
Harper was a productive, composed high school guard who drew comparisons to Jalen Brunson at the time with his size, production and facilitation skills. He shared MVP honors at the 2024 McDonald's All American Game before averaging 19 points as a Rutgers freshman and earning third-team All-Big Ten honors. The San Antonio Spurs selected Harper second in the draft, and he made the All-Rookie team after showing improved playmaking and scoring. In the 2026 NBA Finals, he averaged 18 points, 6.4 rebounds and three assists. Harper's strengths lie in his perimeter versatility, and he has the potential to be an All-Star at either the point guard, shooting guard or small forward position.

Previous No. 2: Ace Bailey

3. VJ Edgecombe, SG

2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 3
Edgecombe improved rapidly throughout high school, emerging as a dynamic transition finisher with NBA-level athleticism, scoring ability and a high basketball IQ. articles.headline: Longtime Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter dies
articles.description: Lawrence Tanter had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days until his retirement in June following a stroke.
articles.body:
Longtime Los Angeles Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter has died, the team announced Wednesday.

"We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter," the team wrote in a statement shared on its social media accounts. "For 43 years, LT's voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family."

In June, the 76-year-old Tanter retired from his courtside post where he had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days of the 1980s.

Tanter had suffered a stroke late in the regular season and missed the Lakers' last six home games, plus the playoffs.

Last month, shortly before entering into hospice care, Tanter texted ESPN.

"Quote me," he wrote, "'It's been a blessing.'"

Known by Lakers fans simply by his initials, LT, Tanter was the longest-tenured PA announcer in team history and was recognized for his style as much as for his longevity.

Despite being equipped with a booming baritone voice and an imposing 6-foot-7 frame, Tanter's presentation relied on restraint, using a silky-smooth delivery to share the Lakers' starting lineups, substitutions, fouls and score announcements with an aim to inform rather than distract the audience.

Tanter channeled his parallel career as a disc jockey at various jazz radio stations in L.A. when he reported to the arena, often wearing an eight-panel cap atop his head and sporting a well-manicured white goatee on his chin.

Always part of the tapestry but never stealing the spotlight, Tanter's signature call became announcing "The Laker girlllssss" when the dance team finished a routine and scampered off the court.

Tanter's role was particularly poignant during the Lakers' most recent championship season in 2019-20. When the Lakers played their first game after Kobe Bryant's death in January 2020, Tanter introduced all five Lakers starters with the same line: "6-6, 20th year out of Lower Merion High School, Kob-eeeeee Bryant!" Later that season, when the Lakers competed in the NBA bubble in Orlando, Florida, and eventually won the championship, Tanter recorded player introductions at a home studio in the Porter Ranch area of Los Angeles that were played before Lakers games at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex.

The Chicago native played forward for his high school basketball team and received a scholarship to attend the University of Dubuque in Iowa.

He went on to be a part of 10 Lakers championships and 16 Western Conference titles.

"Lawrence Tanter has been an integral part of the Lakers gameday experience for more than four decades, setting the tone for countless memorable moments with his professionalism, energy and signature booming voice," Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss said in June when Tanter was shifting to an advisory role. articles.headline: How to bet Falcons-Packers on TNF: Analysis, tips and top plays
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Falcons-Packers on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
"Thursday Night Football" features the Atlanta Falcons visiting Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers. With Michael Penix Jr. healthy and slated to start, the Falcons get some stability at the quarterback position. Off to an 0-2 start, behind an offense that couldn't find any sense of rhythm with No. 3 QB Cooper Rush taking snaps, we finally get to see how coach Kevin Stefanski schemes for his two playmakers in the pass game -- Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. -- versus a Packers defense that is playing zone coverage on 70.5% of opponent dropbacks.

Now, Stefanski's call sheet will be based off the volume for running back Bijan Robinson, who is averaging 18.5 carries per game. We should see a lot of outside zone schemes (which should mirror the play-action passing game) versus a Green Bay defense allowing only 2.9 YPC (second fewest in the league) through the first two weeks.

For the Packers, quarterback Jordan Love has completed only 52.1% of his passes to start the season, but he has hit on eight explosive-play throws (20 or more yards), which ranks fifth in the league. Christian Watson is a big-play target who has scored three touchdowns through two weeks, while Matthew Golden is emerging as a go-to option. It's a committee approach in the backfield, one that lacks difference-making ability.

Betting outlook

Looking at a line that has dropped to Green Bay -4.5, I'm going to take the Packers to cover the spread (and a moneyline bet), plus I'm hitting the over at 42.5. I like Love and the Green Bay pass game against a Falcons defense that struggled in Week 2 versus the Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young (287 yards, three touchdowns). Expect more rhythm throws to the middle of the field, plus the isolation shots to Watson. And I think Green Bay can get enough out of this makeshift backfield (Kaleb Johnson flashed on tape last week) to sustain and control tempo. Plus, I'm betting on that Packers defense to win enough early-down situations to keep the Falcons' offense off schedule based on the game plan. We know Robinson will get his touches, and there will be schemed throws for Penix to hit based on Stefanski's history as a playcaller. But I don't think it's enough to cover or knock off the Packers at the home opener at Lambeau Field.

Total points UNDER 42.5 (-108)

Ben Solak: The Falcons finally get functional quarterback play with Penix healthy and stepping in, but he was not even an average starter when we last saw him and now takes snaps in a new offense and having seen no preseason action. I'm expecting plenty of rust against a solid Packers defense. On the other side of the ball, DC Jeff Ulbrich remains a quality designer of pressure packages -- something with which the Packers' young and injury-riddled O-line is likely to struggle. I see sacks, punts and field goals in this one.
